svg.text: MB102 830-point breadboard · ESP32 38-pin + dual relay + 2 pumps · every wire goes to the hole shown · same circuit as the schematic · 5.5 k resistors · relay: jumper ON, VCC on 5 V
ESP32-DevKitC (38-pin): USB end on the right, antenna end on the left - keep the antenna end over bare plastic, no wires over it
its plug goes into the jack
HOW THE ESP32 SITS ON THE BREADBOARD (one column, looking from above)
A = ESP32 upper pin row (D23, D22, D21, D4): no free hole - use the pin tip
B-H hidden under the board - not usable
I = ESP32 lower pin row (3V3, D34, D35, D25, D26, D27, GND, 5V)
J = FREE ROW: solid jumpers for the lower-row pins go here (same column as the pin)
solid-core jumper (both ends plug into holes)
Dupont wire (black end on the module, male end in the hole)
Dupont F-F wire onto the ESP32 pin tip
dashed = optional or remove-when-USB wire black badge = wire number in the table
Board: MB102 830-point = 63 columns. Holes A-E (above the groove) are joined
down each column; F-J (below the groove) likewise. The groove splits the two.
Rails: bottom outer = +5V, bottom inner = GND, top inner = +3V3, top outer =
GND (joined to the bottom GND by wire 3). Ignore the +/- printed on the board;
if a rail has a gap in the middle, bridge it with a jumper.
ESP32 fit: its two pin rows are 1.0 in apart, so it fills rows A..I. Row J is the
only free row, so every pin on the lower row (3V3, D34.. D25 .. D27, GND, 5V)
gets a SOLID-CORE jumper in row J. The upper row (D23, D22, D21, D4) has no
free hole: push a female Dupont end onto the pin tip (wires 36,37,41,42).
Wire types: SOLID jumper = bare breadboard wire; DUPONT = male end in a
hole, female end on the module (black housing on the module end).
Row letters here may be printed reversed (J at top) on your board - just
keep 'above the groove' / 'below the groove' the same as in the picture.
Photos are not to scale and the relay NO / NC screws may be swapped on your
board - COM is always the middle screw; NO is the one that is open when the
relay is off. Test with the a / b pump commands, swap the two pump leads if
pump A and pump B come out the wrong way round.
WIRING TABLE - tick each wire off as you go (numbers match the black badges)
ESP32: pin rows in A and I, 3V3/GND end in col 36 (USB toward col 55)
R1 5.5k G20-G24 R2 5.5k I24 > GND rail R3 5.5k G5-G9
R4a 5.5k F9-F13 R4b 5.5k I13 > GND rail R5 5.5k A59 > 3V3 rail (top)
470uF cap: + leg > +5V rail c23, striped leg > GND rail c23
DC jack red > 5V rail (bottom outer) c3
DC jack black > GND rail (bottom inner) c4
GND rail (bottom inner) c61 > GND rail (top outer) c61
hole J49 > GND rail (bottom inner) c49
Turbidity GND > GND rail (bottom inner) c22
Flow sensor red > 5V rail (bottom outer) c7
Flow sensor black > GND rail (bottom inner) c6
Relay GND > GND rail (bottom inner) c15
Pump A black > GND rail (bottom inner) c25
Pump B black > GND rail (bottom inner) c29
OLED GND > GND rail (top outer) c33
DS18B20 black > GND rail (top outer) c58
ESP32 D23 tip > GND rail (top outer) c39

Photos: Components101 (ESP32-DevKitC, relay, YF-S201), DFRobot (TDS, turbidity), SparkFun (DS18B20, DC jack), Adafruit (pump, adapter), Makerguides (OLED). Product photos belong to their owners; used here as a personal build aid.
